speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my clinic. I understand you have been suffering from chronic pain in your left shoulder without any history of trauma. To help me narrow down the cause, could you describe exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements make it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy/Impingement Syndrome

Thank you for that detailed history; the combination of age, insidious onset, and pain worsening with extreme range of motion is very suggestive of rotator cuff pathology. Given your diabetes, which can predispose you to neuropathic changes, and the fact that this is affecting your daily life, I need to confirm if there is any weakness when lifting your arm.

REQUEST TEST: Serum inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP)
REQUEST TEST: Shoulder_Ultrasound
